projection: Around 2 hours of real projection, with moderate sillage after that
review: A 2025 Ard Al Zaafaran release, and there is only one Naif — the earlier name confusion is resolved. Sweetened plum, cinnamon and cardamom over bergamot, an artemisia-lavender-davana heart, and a tonka-labdanum-benzoin base. A spicy-sweet amber for cool weather and dressed-up occasions, not the casual scent it was first filed as.
layering: If it reads too dense or sweet, layer with a clean citrus or dry cedar. Avoid pairing it with another strong oud or amber.
consensus: Too new for a published Fragrantica or Parfumo score — the pages were not retrievable. Retailer and wearer descriptions are positive: bold, rich and mysterious, with good lasting power on fabric.

name: Throne Eclipse
inspiration: Althair / Clive Christian Blonde Amber-style hybrid (medium confidence, unconfirmed)
projection: Noticeable to strong in the opening; sillage moderate-to-strong in cool weather
review: Spicy-fruity apple, clove and cardamom opening; cinnamon, lavender and geranium give aromatic structure; the drydown is the main event - vanilla and amber dominant over cedar. Reports say the opening hints at Blonde Amber while the later wear leans Althair.
layering: Dry cedar adds structure; a small citrus layer cuts the amber density. Avoid another amber, cinnamon or vanilla-heavy scent.
flag: Can open as a dense amber bomb; redundant if you already own Althair or Liquid Brun
consensus: Fragrantica 4.58/5 from 64 votes, 15 reviews. Praised for quality, warmth and value. Parfumo reviewers split between "hints of both" and "neither" - treat the hybrid label as medium confidence.

name: Regent
base: Musk, Cedarwood, Sandalwood, Ambergris, Patchouli, Tonka
review: 2026 Maison Asrar release — a bright citrus-led fresh with grapefruit-ginger-bergamot opening into an orange blossom and orris heart, settling on musk-cedarwood-sandalwood. Community loves the DNA and freshness but longevity is the known pain point: some report barely 2–3 hours on first use. Community tip is to let the bottle rest for maceration after opening. At its price point the citrus freshness is lovely, but be prepared to top up.

name: Vanguard
top: Pineapple, Blackcurrant, Grapefruit, Pink Pepper, Apple, Bergamot
heart: Cardamom, Lily of the Valley, Ginger, Carnation
base: Musk, Cashmere Musk, Ambergris, Leather, Cedarwood, Moss
review: Aventus-adjacent fruity chypre from Maison Asrar with a polarising reception. Opens with a bright pineapple-blackcurrant-grapefruit bomb over pink pepper; carnation and lily of the valley add florality in the heart; leather-moss-ambergris lands the drydown in classic chypre territory. The 'light airy top meeting dark moss and leather base' is the distinctive DNA. Performance is batch-variable — some report 7–8 hours, others find the musk dominates early. Reportedly improves significantly with 1–3 months of maceration post-opening.

name: Egra Men
review: Community consensus puts Egra Men among the best Creed GIT dupes at its price point — a cool, fresh fougère blending the citrus-violet-lavender DNA of GIT with faint Cool Water vibes. Opens on clean bergamot and grapefruit fizz, transitions to an iris-violet heart, dries down to soft sandalwood and musk. Performance divides opinion: 8–10 hours on some skin, moderate-then-skin-scent after 4 hours in heat. At under $30, the risk-to-reward is exceptional.

name: Rafan pour Homme
review: Community consistently calls Rafan one of the most faithful Le Sel d'Issey alternatives — many can't distinguish the two in blind tests, calling it 95% of the original. Opens with a striking salty-ginger accord; seaweed-vetiver adds a green, mineral edge in the heart; cedar-oakmoss grounds the finish in clean wood. Longevity impresses for an aquatic, often outlasting the original's modest EdT. The consensus go-to dupe for the sea-salt-in-a-bottle experience at a fraction of the Issey price.

name: Le Sel d'Issey
inspiration: Original Issey Miyake release — not a clone
longevity: Upper end of the EDT range — still detectable after about 6 hours
projection: Moderate; mineral and dry rather than expansive
review: A salty mineral aquatic — sea salt and ginger over seaweed and vetiver, drying to cedar and oakmoss. Warm skin after a swim: marine without going dirty, and kept dry and masculine by the mossy-woody base. Editions now run EDT (2024), EDP (2025) and Parfum (2026).
layering: Best alone. A clean musk lifts the salt without muddying the oakmoss.
consensus: Divisive by design — Fragrantica ran a piece on it splitting opinion. In a direct six-person comparison against Goldfield & Banks Ingenious Ginger, all six preferred the Ingenious Ginger, though they liked both. Different scents entirely: this one is salty-woody-marine.

name: Summer in Dubai
base: Tonka Bean, Patchouli, Ambroxan, Amber, Musk
review: Anfar 1950's care-free aromatic aquatic that punches well above its price point. Grapefruit and pineapple open with sea-spray freshness over bergamot; cardamom and ginger add spice without heat; ambroxan and tonka extend the trail into a clean, warm drydown. Community praises performance as exceptional for the price — 6–8 hours with strong projection. Called 'an absolute belter' and a consistent compliment getter. A summer daily driver.

name: Anfar Zenit Nomad
review: Anfar 1950's Zenit Series entry — described by reviewers as 'legendary.' Lemon-pineapple-bergamot open with pink pepper brightness; birch and oud create a smoky, woody heart lifted by rosemary and white amber; vanilla, leather, and vetiver ground the drydown in a complex animalic trail. Community advice: 2 sprays maximum — this is potent. Performance reports are extraordinary, with some clocking 24+ hours. Exceptional value in the Anfar Zenit line; a full-day commitment in a bottle.

name: Armaf Odyssey Limoni
inspiration: LV Freshie DNA — Afternoon Swim / Pacific Chill adjacent (not a 1:1 clone)
review: Bright, realistic iced-tea-and-lemons freshie — an amalgamation of the LV freshie DNAs rather than one accurate clone. Punches well above its price for compliments on hot days, but longevity is the clear weakness, fading to a skin scent inside a couple of hours.
layering: Use as a lemon-tea topper over {Turathi Blue} or {Aquatica} to refresh a fading citrus opening.
consensus: Bright, realistic iced-tea-and-lemons freshie — an amalgamation of the LV freshie DNAs rather than one accurate clone. Punches well above its price for compliments on hot days, but longevity is the clear weakness, fading to a skin scent inside a couple of hours.

name: Afnan Supremacy Not Only Intense
inspiration: Creed Aventus (earthy Tom Ford Ombre Leather drydown)
review: Extrait de parfum (30%+ oil) built on the Aventus fruity-chypre idea but not a 1:1 clone — the oakmoss-patchouli heart dries down closer to Ombre Leather's earthy leather. Rich, versatile, and a genuine single-signature contender at the price.
layering: Layer {Qaed Al Fursan} over the top to inject a juicy pineapple lift into the leathery drydown.
consensus: Extrait de parfum (30%+ oil) built on the Aventus fruity-chypre idea but not a 1:1 clone — the oakmoss-patchouli heart dries down closer to Ombre Leather's earthy leather. Rich, versatile, and a genuine single-signature contender at the price.

name: Luxe Street
review: Maison Alhambra's Luxe-line rendition of Bond No. 9 Lafayette Street — community pegs it around 80% for the money. Sweet apple over an ambroxan-vanilla-tonka base makes it an approachable, cosy fruity-oriental for cooler evenings.
flag: ⚠️ Performance unverified — update longevity/projection after first wear.
consensus: Maison Alhambra's Luxe-line rendition of Bond No. 9 Lafayette Street — community pegs it around 80% for the money. Sweet apple over an ambroxan-vanilla-tonka base makes it an approachable, cosy fruity-oriental for cooler evenings.

name: Legesi
inspiration: Chanel Egoiste Platinum / Bleu de Chanel (softened barbershop twist)
review: Heavily-inspired Platinum Egoiste woody-aromatic softened with a vintage-fougère barbershop drydown and a touch of BdC. Projects well the first two hours. Known quirk: the opening 15-45 min can read harsh and slightly metallic before it settles into the clean shave-soap base.
consensus: Heavily-inspired Platinum Egoiste woody-aromatic softened with a vintage-fougère barbershop drydown and a touch of BdC. Projects well the first two hours. Known quirk: the opening 15-45 min can read harsh and slightly metallic before it settles into the clean shave-soap base.

name: Cosmic Giardino
review: 80-90% Paradise Garden with its own twist — sweeter and smoother than the original, leaning into lavender-violet-geranium and a salty coconut-fig freshness over a soft woody-tonka base. A juicy, slightly green summer crowd-pleaser.
layering: Pairs with {Aquatica} to deepen the coconut into a fuller tropical-beach accord.
consensus: 80-90% Paradise Garden with its own twist — sweeter and smoother than the original, leaning into lavender-violet-geranium and a salty coconut-fig freshness over a soft woody-tonka base. A juicy, slightly green summer crowd-pleaser.

name: Mercedes-Benz Club Black
review: A genuinely well-regarded designer original (not a clone). Bright bergamot flashes then gives way to smoky incense and jasmine over a rich, lightly caramelised vanilla-benzoin base that surrounds rather than shouts. A polished night/date scent that smells far above its price.
layering: Layer under {Khamrah Qahwa} for a smoky incense-coffee-vanilla evening cloud.
consensus: A genuinely well-regarded designer original (not a clone). Bright bergamot flashes then gives way to smoky incense and jasmine over a rich, lightly caramelised vanilla-benzoin base that surrounds rather than shouts. A polished night/date scent that smells far above its price.

name: Afnan Rare Reef
top: Orange, Mint, Citron, Grapefruit, Blackcurrant, Coriander
review: Inspired by LV Pacific Chill but taken sweeter, fruitier and more citrus-forward — bright, beachy and clean with an apricot-fig warmth in the base. Not an exact clone (Pacific Chill is smoother and more apricot-heavy); reviews split on the synthetic citrus edge but praise the value.
layering: Layer over {Aquatica} to push a brighter citrus sparkle over the creamy coconut base.
consensus: Inspired by LV Pacific Chill but taken sweeter, fruitier and more citrus-forward — bright, beachy and clean with an apricot-fig warmth in the base. Not an exact clone (Pacific Chill is smoother and more apricot-heavy); reviews split on the synthetic citrus edge but praise the value.

name: Azul
longevity: Contested — retailer reviews claim 6–8 hours, individual Fragrantica reviewers report as little as 1
projection: Moderate to strong and noticeably fresh up front, then it drops away
layering: One spray of a clean musk or light citrus underneath. If it is thin, add a dry cedar or ambroxan scent; if it is sharp, soften it with a simple musk or light vanilla.
review: Free gift with the order, and it turns out to be a Dior Homme Cologne clone — FragrantSouq puts it at 90–95% similarity. An "icy lemonade" opening with brighter lemon than the original, into clean musk and sandalwood. Good value even before you count that it was free.
flag: Longevity is the open question — reports run from 1 to 8 hours. Measure it yourself.
consensus: Widely called one of the better clones available: fresh, bright, energetic, easy to like, and far cheaper than Dior Homme Cologne. The consistent criticism is inconsistent longevity across skin types. Fragrantica and Parfumo vote counts were not retrievable.

name: Ravine Ice
longevity: 4–7 hours — typically 6–7 on skin, longer on fabric; a minority report only 2–3
projection: Moderate at the opening, then a close within-a-foot trail
layering: Partners naturally with {Ravine Ginger} — Ice brightens Ginger, Ginger gives Ice body. Also works over clean musk, citrus or a light cedar.
review: CONFIRMED the Pacific Rock Moss dupe — community puts it around 90% of the Goldfield & Banks original, slightly less dense and more transparent. Salty lemon soap over icy herbaceous mineral: lemon-geranium opening, sage-lavender-salt heart, moss-cedar-ambroxan base. This is why the Pacific Rock Moss clone target came off the wishlist.
consensus: The Last Spritz scores it 87/100; a 2025 release with positive forum reception. Praise: the Pacific Rock Moss likeness at a fraction of the price, and the clean salty-mineral character. Gripe: performance varies widely by skin — some get 6–7 hours, some only 2–3.

name: Ravine Ginger
base: Vanilla, Amber, Sandalwood, Cashmere, Patchouli, Musk
longevity: About 7 hours. The Goldfield & Banks original averaged 7 h 22 m across 47 testers — roughly 4 hours of real presence, then 3+ as a skin scent, and 12–15 hours on cloth
projection: Moderate and deliberate — within arm’s length for the first 90 minutes, then a personal aura. Confident rather than loud, and office-safe
layering: One spray under one or two of {Ravine Ice}. Also clean citrus, dry cedar, light vanilla or soft musk.
review: An Ingenious Ginger clone, and reviewers call it dead-on — about $54 against roughly $148–240 for the Goldfield & Banks. IMPORTANT: the "ginger" is GINGER FLOWER, a soft powdery magnolia-adjacent floral, not culinary ginger root. That is why it reads sunny and creamy rather than spicy: luminous mandarin and lemon peel, a magnolia-jasmine heart, then vanilla, amber and Australian sandalwood. Pairs with {Ravine Ice} — French Avenue’s Ravine line is doing Goldfield & Banks.
consensus: Fragrantica 4.4/5 from 72 votes; the original scores 8.4/10 at ScentGrade. Consistently rated broadly pleasant and well balanced with no synthetic harshness. Main gripe is the quiet, close-to-skin projection.

name: Night Club Green Tweed
heart: Violet leaf, violet, iris, soft aromatic greenery
base: Sandalwood, ambergris-style mineral musk, dry woods
longevity: Likely moderate to good; batch and skin dependent
projection: Noticeable in the opening, then moderate
layering: Use it alone first. For more lift add a light citrus or neroli underneath; if it feels too green, soften it with clean musk or a restrained sandalwood. One spray of the layer is enough.
review: The clearest clone in the order and the best price-to-risk buy at $14 for 50 ml. Green aromatic fougère with the recognisable GIT structure — bright lemony-green opening, violet/iris heart, clean mineral-woody drydown.
consensus: The budget-clone pattern is broadly positive: recognisable green freshness, versatility and value. Gripes are a sharper, more synthetic opening than the original and batch-variable performance.

name: Jacques Yves Tempete
base: Iso E Super, White Musk, Java Vetiver Oil, Patchouli
longevity: Contested — Fragrantica scores it 2.0/5, while retailers and some wearers claim 10+ hours and say it improves after the bottle has sat for a few weeks
projection: Fragrantica sillage 3.0/5; described elsewhere as a sharp, mineral trail
layering: Clean musk, light citrus or dry cedar. It is already mineral, so avoid another aquatic — the result can go metallic.
review: The $19 buy turns out to be an Orage clone — four independent retailers list it as inspired by Louis Vuitton Orage. Bergamot-grapefruit opening over an iris-hedione-pepper heart, into Iso E Super, vetiver and patchouli. Strong value if the performance lands on your skin.
flag: Longevity reports are wildly split (2/5 on Fragrantica vs 10+ hours claimed) — measure it yourself before trusting either.
consensus: Reads as a solid mid-tier pick with broad appeal; ratings run 3.2–4.07/5 depending on platform, and value and presentation both score around 4/5. Praise: a strong cheap alternative to Orage with a fresh, vital opening. Criticism: genuinely inconsistent longevity between wearers.

name: Jungle Vibe
heart: Fig (fig leaf accord), Green Notes, Aquatic Notes
longevity: About 7 hours on skin — comparable to the Dries Van Noten original, which Parfumo scores 7.5/10 from 126 ratings
projection: Moderate; Fragrantica sillage 3.0/5, present for the first 2–3 hours without being intrusive
layering: Clean musk, citrus or a light aquatic. If it is too green, dry it down with cedar or vetiver. Keep the second fragrance to one spray.
review: A Santal Greenery clone — ScentMetric puts it at 78% similar, and wearers call it a slightly more citrusy reading with a bigger bergamot kick. Grapefruit-bergamot opening, milky-creamy fig with green violet-leaf crispness, smooth sandalwood and white musk underneath. About $25 against roughly $250 for the Dries Van Noten, at comparable longevity.
consensus: Confirmed dupe in community comparisons. The original holds Parfumo 7.6/10 from 161 ratings and is widely called nicer, smoother and cleaner — but not ten-times-the-price nicer. Jungle Vibe itself scores Fragrantica 3.0/5 on both longevity and sillage; reception is positive-but-mixed and explicitly not for everyone.

name: Cedrus Blanc
base: Cedarwood, White Musk (retailers also list Vanilla)
longevity: Parfumo 7.77/10 from 8 ratings. The CH original runs 4–8 hours and settles to a skin scent inside 2–3 — expect the same shape
projection: Parfumo sillage 7.48/10 from 8 ratings; soft to moderate, intimate rather than expansive
layering: Citrus or clean musk for lift, or a restrained amber for warmth. {Night Club Green Tweed} adds texture — one spray only, or the woody accord gets crowded.
review: A CH Cedar Chic clone (Private Blends AU) — near-identical structure: aldehydes and bergamot, orange blossom, then white musk and cedar. The original is Antoine Maisondieu’s "expensive freshly-laundered cotton" idea, and despite the name the cedar is subtle; one reviewer renamed it "Aldehyde Chic". Reads like a perfectly tailored white shirt. About $25 against roughly $400 for the Herrera.
consensus: Community treats it as a confirmed dupe — the note structures line up almost exactly and both give the high-end-spa aura. Parfumo 7.77 longevity / 7.48 sillage, but from only 8 ratings, so treat the numbers as provisional. Criticism: some find it too soapy or too musky.

name: Fareed
inspiration: YSL La Nuit de L’Homme EDT
longevity: Mixed — Parfumo 7.1/10; reports range from a few hours to better than the original
projection: Moderate; some report a stronger opening than the original
layering: Clean musk or light cedar to reinforce the polished side, and a restrained vanilla for warmth. Avoid another cardamom-heavy scent.
review: Cardamom-led spicy-fresh woody with a clean, slightly soapy lavender/geranium facet over tonka and wood. Best treated as a fresher, cleaner interpretation of La Nuit rather than a one-to-one clone.
consensus: Parfumo 8.3/10 from 124 ratings. Praise: recognisable La Nuit DNA, cardamom quality, low price. Gripes: a soapier twist and variable performance.

name: Mosaic
inspiration: YSL MYSLF / MYSLF L’Absolu-adjacent (community mapping, not an official claim)
longevity: Described as above average, but there is not enough independent wear data for a firm number
layering: Clean musk or light citrus to extend the fresh side, dry cedar to cut the hygienic sweetness. Avoid another orange-blossom scent.
review: A 2026 Maze Collection release. Bright spicy-citrus opening, clean orange-blossom and orris heart, airy woody-amber drydown — a softer, airier take on the MYSLF idea.
flag: Clone mapping is community-based, medium confidence
consensus: Fragrantica 4.70/5 from about 20 votes — too small to be stable. Risk: the clean musk effect can read detergent-like.

name: Nazih Silver
longevity: Moderate to good; varies by version and skin
projection: Noticeable in the opening, then moderate
layering: Light vanilla or clean cedar to reinforce the sweet woody base, or a citrus-musk to brighten it. Avoid another cinnamon-heavy scent.
review: Crisp apple-citrus over cinnamon, clove and geranium into vanilla, sandalwood and cedar. Sold under two house labels for the same general target — compare prices before buying.
flag: Target is Boss Bottled Intense, NOT Silver Mountain Water (earlier speculation corrected)
consensus: Fragrantica 4.03/5 from 33 votes. Praise: the recognisable Boss Bottled Intense direction and value. Gripes: an oily or sharp opening, and close-in-style rather than an exact match.

name: Hawas Fire
inspiration: Gissah Imperial Valley-style twist, unconfirmed; its own Hawas Fire DNA is also plausible
projection: Noticeable, especially in the opening; sillage 7.9/10 — use cautiously indoors
layering: Dry cedar or clean musk if the marine accord feels sharp. Avoid another loud aquatic or ambergris scent until its projection is known.
review: A 2025 Hawas flanker, and not the fruit bomb the name suggests — aromatic saline opening, marine jasmine heart, warm mineral ambergris base. "Fire" means density in the base, not cinnamon or vanilla.
flag: Sample first — not a safe blind buy if the goal is a known clone
consensus: Fragrantica 4.37/5 from about 2,015 votes; Parfumo 7.8/10 from 164. Praise: freshness, presence, mineral character. Gripes: some find it generic, too marine, or less fiery than expected.

name: Ombre D’Or
inspiration: Matière Première Crystal Saffron-style (community, medium-high confidence)
heart: Saffron, metallic notes, Damascus rose, iris
longevity: Generally strong, though some wearers report a shorter or quieter result
projection: Noticeable to strong in the opening; sillage moderate to strong
layering: Clean musk or a little citrus for air, and dry cedar to make it more wearable. Avoid another saffron, iris or incense-heavy scent.
review: 75 ml. Sharp metallic saffron opening with lime and musk, an iris and rose centre, then a resinous incense-and-woods drydown that keeps the mineral saffron signature. Polished and austere rather than a sweet amber.
flag: Polarising — sample first even at a low price; poor value if the collection already has several saffron ambers
consensus: Praise: the Crystal Saffron resemblance, the unusual metallic saffron effect, and value. Gripes: harsh, synthetic, too metallic, less smooth than the niche original.

name: Odyssey Ba Ha Mas
inspiration: Tropical-aquatic original profile; loose Creed Virgin Island Water comparison only
top: Asian pear, plum, Granny Smith apple, cantaloupe melon, salt, marine algae
heart: Aquatic notes, water lily, oakmoss, frankincense
longevity: Likely moderate — independent data is limited
projection: Moderate, most noticeable in the fruity-aquatic opening
layering: Clean musk, citrus or a little coconut. Dry cedar reduces the sweet fruit effect. Avoid another marine fragrance initially.
review: Fruity, salty and watery rather than a straight coconut scent — a tropical aquatic that is not just another blue. Good discovery value if that is what you want; skip it if you need coconut or a recognisable niche clone.
flag: Clone confidence low — no official target
consensus: Too new and under-reviewed for a stable number. Likely gripe: a drydown more generic than the opening.

name: Odyssey Nexus
inspiration: Giorgio Armani Acqua di Giò Profumo-style (retailer and community, medium-high confidence)
longevity: Moderate in early reports — expect a workday, not beast mode
projection: Noticeable in the opening, then moderate
layering: Clean musk or light citrus to amplify the freshness, and a restrained dry cedar to reinforce the base. Avoid another incense-heavy aquatic.
review: Citrus-marine opening with a greener aromatic heart than a shower-gel blue, then the smoky, resinous depth that drives the Profumo comparison. One of the safer wishlist picks if you miss discontinued Profumo.
consensus: Fragrantica 4.73/5 from about 22 votes and 8 reviews — an early sample. Praise: the Profumo-like incense, freshness and value. Caveat: too recent to judge batch consistency.

name: Dynasty
inspiration: Clive Christian L Red Tea Vetiver-style, unconfirmed
top: Bergamot, ginger, clary sage, nutmeg, raspberry
longevity: Likely moderate to good — independent data is limited
projection: Moderate, with the spice and amberwood most noticeable early
layering: Clean citrus to lift the opening or dry cedar to deepen the base; a restrained vanilla softens the suede. Avoid another tea or cashmeran-heavy scent.
review: Citrus-ginger-nutmeg opening with a tart raspberry accent, a dry rooibos-and-suede centre, and a warm textured amberwood trail — no syrupy vanilla base. An older database "Dynasty" is a name collision; use the current Lattafa product.
consensus: Still lightly reviewed. Praise: the tea and suede character and niche-style value. Caution: some describe it as an original composition rather than a clone.

name: Zenith Santal
inspiration: Emporio Armani Stronger With You Sandalwood
longevity: Generally above average in community reports
projection: Noticeable to strong for the first several hours; sillage moderate to strong in cooler air
layering: Dry cedar for structure or a little citrus for lift. Avoid another sweet amber or sandalwood gourmand.
review: Saffron lift into a sweet chestnut and lavender heart, then a creamy sandalwood-vanilla drydown kept in check by cedar. Note this is NOT a Santal 33-style scent.
flag: Do not record it as Le Labo Santal 33 — the target is Stronger With You Sandalwood
consensus: Fragrantica 4.43/5 from 324 votes; Parfumo 8.2/10 from 60. Unusually consistent praise for the resemblance and performance. Gripe: too sweet or dense in warm weather.

name: Mawj Moscow Mule
inspiration: By Kilian Blue Moon Ginger Dash
longevity: Commonly reported around all-day freshness, but skin-variable
projection: Moderate, strongest in the citrus-ginger opening
layering: Clean musk, light cedar or a dry ginger scent. A restrained vanilla softens sharpness — keep the application light.
review: Bright lemon and bergamot with spicy ginger, a cool minty-cypress heart, and a transparent ozonic-mossy finish. The Blue Moon original is a Blue Lagoon cocktail idea — lemon, calone, mint and aldehydes over vodka and ginger, into ambroxan and white musk — so it is an aquatic-citrus cocktail scent, genuinely distinct from the floral-amber {Ravine Ginger}.
consensus: Praise: the refreshing ginger-citrus character and the unusual Blue Moon profile. Gripes: sharpness, a synthetic lemon effect, and the cocktail impression fading into plain clean musk. The By Kilian original draws split reviews too — "refined clarity" for some, a screechy opening and boozy musk for others.

name: Obsidian
longevity: Roughly 5–8 hours on skin, sometimes more — not guaranteed beast mode
projection: A strong opening is commonly reported, then moderate
layering: Clean musk or a small citrus layer to brighten it, and dry cedar to reinforce the structure. Avoid another iris, leather or oud-heavy scent.
review: Bright orange over a powdery iris accord, a leather and rose heart, and a warm woody drydown with the iris running through it. Record the 2025 qualifier — do not collapse it into plain "Dior Homme Parfum".
consensus: Fragrantica about 4.40/5 from roughly 1,100 votes and 177 reviews. Praise: the DHP resemblance, attractive iris, value. Gripes: a sharper opening and variable skin longevity.

name: The One EDP (Men)
inspiration: Original designer release — not a clone
projection: Moderate, with a noticeable opening that becomes intimate
layering: Usually best alone. A clean musk extends the soft aura and a dry cedar adds structure. Avoid another cardamom or tobacco scent.
review: Citrusy-spicy aromatic opening, a warm luminous cardamom and ginger heart, and a smooth intimate tobacco-amber-cedar drydown. Buy it for refinement and versatility, not projection. The women’s The One EDP is a different product — keep the records separate.
consensus: Durably positive on scent quality and date-night appeal. Common gripe: performance feels underpowered if you expect a large trail.

name: Kenzo Homme Eau de Parfum
inspiration: Original designer release — not a clone. Kenzo Homme EDP (2022), by Quentin Bisch.
layering: Best alone — the leather-patchouli base does not want company. A clean musk can stretch the marine top if you want it fresher.
review: Edition settled: this is the 2022 Eau de Parfum, the black bamboo flacon. Main accords marine, leather, patchouli, aromatic, animalic — a salty marine opening laid over leather and patchouli, darker and more linear than the rest of the line. Day and night, close to even, with a slight night lean. Note the line was rebuilt in 2021–22 and the editions are barely related: the 1991 original EDT (reissued 2022) is the classic aquatic, EDT Intense 2021 is the fig-woody fresh one, Marine 2023 is the summer-weight version.
consensus: Fragrantica 4.3/5 from 2,497 votes — a solid, well-established sample. 8 h longevity and strong sillage. Community reads it as linear but distinctive; the marine-over-leather effect is the draw.

name: Blue for Him
inspiration: Original Kenneth Cole Blue for Him EDT; not a confirmed clone
longevity: Likely moderate to close for the EDT — independent data is limited
projection: Moderate in the opening, then quieter
layering: Clean musk or citrus for lift. It is already a simple freshie — keep any layer to one spray.
review: Bright citrus-fruit opening with pineapple giving a sweeter edge than a standard blue, a clean ginger-lavender-marine heart, and a dry, lightly warm cedar-vetiver-amber finish. An easy casual daily scent at the right price.
flag: Other Kenneth Cole Blue flankers exist — confirm the bottle is Blue for Him EDT
consensus: An established casual designer freshie, but the review sample is too thin for a meaningful number. Likely gripe: a generic blue effect and limited longevity next to modern clones.

name: Jean Lowe Verde Aura
top: Blackcurrant, coriander, mint, lemon, citron, orange
longevity: Mixed - reports range from about 5 to 8+ hours
projection: Strong at the opening, then moderate and fading fairly quickly
layering: Clean musk or light woods smooth the herbal edge; a small citrus layer reinforces freshness. Avoid another green or mint-heavy scent.
review: Sharp cool citrus-herbal opening with mint and coriander, softened by basil and apricot, finishing warm and lightly musky on fig, dates and ambrette. Stays fresh rather than sweet - a convincing Cactus Garden mood at budget money.
flag: Polarising - some skins get sour/pickle/soapy facets; several reviewers dispute the published pyramid
consensus: Fragrantica 4.31/5 from ~77 votes. Praised for the Cactus Garden likeness and unusual green freshness; criticised for polarising sour-herbal and synthetic facets.

name: Maestro
inspiration: Sospiro Il Padrino (high confidence); Triumph of Bacchus / Initio Side Effect adjacent
projection: Strong for the first 2 - 3 hours, then settles
layering: Vanilla or sandalwood softens the leather; a restrained citrus lifts the opening. Avoid another boozy amber or heavy patchouli.
review: Dark, tart and boozy up top - blackcurrant and liquor reading like rich plum. Leather and rose surface in the heart with amber for weight, drying down smooth and resinous on patchouli, vanilla, musk and sandalwood. The clearest Il Padrino alternative on the list.
flag: Leather divides people - sample first if leather or dense patchouli usually overwhelms you
consensus: Small but coherent sample; Parfumo snapshot 8/10 longevity, 9/10 sillage. Praise for the boozy opening, complexity and value; the leather is the main complaint.

name: Maze
inspiration: Azzaro The Most Wanted Parfum-style (tentative, low-medium confidence)
projection: Likely moderate to noticeable given the spice and vanilla structure
layering: Dry cedar cuts the sweetness; a small citrus layer adds lift. Do not pair first with another vanilla, cinnamon or tobacco scent.
review: Cinnamon and cardamom lead with pineapple for controlled sweetness; lavender, cypress and cedar give an aromatic woody backbone; the drydown turns warm and moreish on vanilla and tobacco.
flag: Sample first - clone target and performance are both unestablished
consensus: Too new for a stable consensus. Parfumo has no meaningful rating base and only suggests The Most Wanted Parfum as the nearest comparison.

name: Marmara
inspiration: Purpose 50-style, with Bois Imperial / Ganymede-adjacent facets (medium-low confidence)
projection: Moderate to strong initially, then restrained
layering: Clean musk or citrus brightens the powdery woods; a restrained sandalwood makes it creamier. Avoid another metallic saffron or ambroxan-heavy scent.
review: Sharp peppery saffron/mineral opening, smoothing into a powdery, clean, faintly soapy heart of ambroxan and cashmere wood, then a soft white-sandalwood and musk drydown. Some wearers still catch leather, incense or a Ganymede-like metallic edge.
flag: Not a faithful Purpose 50 copy - hybrid DNA; some report an alcohol/chemical opening
consensus: Fragrantica 4.00/5 from 258 votes, 46 reviews. Praised as original and refined mineral woods; criticised for a chemical opening, vegetal/soapy facets and a drydown too soft for Purpose 50 expectations.

name: Pacific Aura
top: Citron, mint, orange, lemon, blackcurrant, coriander
heart: Apricot, basil, carrot seeds, May rose
longevity: Mixed - praised by some, called short by others
projection: Moderate in the opening, then close to the skin
layering: Clean musk or citrus reinforces the bright opening; light green tea or cedar adds structure. Avoid another apricot or mint-heavy scent.
review: A minty citrus burst over green, tart fruit; basil and apricot soften the heart into the juicy cooling quality Pacific Chill is known for; fig, dates and ambrette leave a lightly sweet musky finish. A summer freshie, not a rich gourmand.
flag: Performance is the weak point - expect reapplication on a hot day
consensus: 18 reviews on the Rayhaan page plus Parfumo agreement on profile: clean freshness and a good Pacific Chill likeness, with at least one explicit longevity complaint.

name: 9PM Night Out
inspiration: Original / hybrid - no settled clone. Facets of JPG Le Beau Le Parfum, Born in Roma Intense, The Most Wanted, Invictus Victory Elixir
top: Dragon fruit, bergamot, cognac, lavender, apple
layering: Dry cedar reduces the sweetness; vanilla reinforces the base but can get dense. Avoid another loud fruity amber.
review: 2026 extrait, not the original 9PM. Dragon fruit, apple, bergamot and cognac open bright and sweet, then suede and toffee darken the heart, closing warm and woody on tonka, patchouli and Ambrofix - much less bubblegum than the original.
flag: Synthetic dragon-fruit opening divides people; narrower mass appeal than Ultra Male or Eros
consensus: Liked for its uniqueness and the smooth toffee-suede drydown; criticised for a synthetic opening and hype above delivery. Reviewers call it an original rather than a clone.

name: Ares
inspiration: Chanel Allure Homme Sport Superleggera-style (medium confidence)
longevity: Parfumo snapshot 7.1/10 from a small sample
layering: Clean musk or citrus extends the fresh side; light cedar adds structure. Avoid another sharp citrus or patchouli-heavy scent.
review: Bright, clean, mandarin-led opening with grapefruit sharpness over a smoother sandalwood/cedar heart; musk, amber and patchouli keep the drydown warmer and less purely citrusy than the first spray.
flag: Velixir pricing is high for a clone - compare cheaper Superleggera-style options first
consensus: Parfumo 7.6/10 from only 11 ratings. Praise for the fresh mandarin opening and versatility; the woody heart reads subdued and musk/patchouli dominate the drydown for some.

name: Le Parfait Pour Homme
inspiration: Creed Green Irish Tweed + Aventus hybrid, leaning GIT (medium-high confidence)
layering: Clean musk or light cedar reinforces the GIT side; a restrained citrus brightens it. Avoid another pineapple-heavy scent.
review: Sharp citrus with tart blackcurrant and a touch of pineapple, a greener floral heart of jasmine, rose and spice, then a warm fruity-woody drydown. Less purely green than Tres Nuit - a GIT/Aventus blend rather than a straight clone of either.
flag: Not the same product as Armaf Tres Nuit; lower priority if you already own Tres Nuit plus a good Aventus clone
consensus: Fragrantica 4.02/5 from 779 votes, 128 reviews. Praised for value, versatility and the unusual GIT/Aventus blend; criticised for synthetic fruit and batch-variable performance.

name: Frostbite
inspiration: Gisada Ambassador-style (medium-high confidence); YSL Y comparisons secondary
heart: Geranium, jasmine, lavender, violet, vetiver, pink pepper
base: Vanilla, amber, ambergris, sandalwood, cedar, patchouli, oakmoss
longevity: 7 - 8 Hours for most, though some find it much weaker
layering: Clean musk smooths the fruit; dry cedar or vetiver makes it more adult. Avoid another fruity blue scent.
review: Bright, sweet and slightly icy - blueberry and mango over citrus and cardamom, a green-spicy floral/vetiver heart, then a warm clean base of vanilla, amber, woods and oakmoss. The blueberry stays detectable throughout.
flag: Conflicting performance reports; the fruit reads synthetic or juvenile to some
consensus: Praised for the unusual blueberry/mango twist and a smoother read on Gisada Ambassador. Some call it 90% Gisada, others a softer original variation.

name: Infinity Silver
top: Bergamot, ginger, grapefruit (some regional pages add pepper and lemon)
layering: Clean musk or citrus extends the fresh side; dry cedar reinforces the woody base. Avoid another rose, ginger or grapefruit-heavy scent.
review: Sparkling grapefruit/bergamot opening with clean ginger, a fruity-spicy heart lifted by an unusual masculine pink rose, and a smooth cedar/vetiver/cashmere base that stays fresh. Often out-performs the discontinued original.
flag: Sometimes confused with "Infinity Black" - the official name is Infinity Silver. Rose is the dividing note.
consensus: Parfumo 8.6/10 from 76 ratings and 9.1/10 for value - the strongest value candidate here. Criticism: synthetic fruit, shower-gel facets and a rough opening.

name: CK One Essence Parfum Intense
inspiration: Original designer release - an intensified reworking of CK One, not a clone
top: White tea, bergamot, blood orange, black pepper
longevity: Better than the original EDT (Calvin Klein claims double the concentration), but still a fresh-tea scent rather than a long-haul performer
projection: Moderate, close to the skin after the first couple of hours
layering: Clean musk or a light citrus extends the tea freshness; dry cedar or sandalwood adds body. Avoid another mint or green-tea scent.
review: Alberto Morillas, 2024. A grown-up rework of CK One: peppery blood orange and bergamot up top, a genuine green/white tea and mint heart, then musk, sandalwood, incense and moss for warmth the original never had. Unisex, easy, office-and-everything wear.
consensus: Broadly positive (Amazon 4.4/5 from ~1,150 reviews). Liked as a more refined, warmer CK One; the usual caveat is that a tea-fresh scent still will not project all day.

name: Just Azraq
inspiration: Rabanne Invictus Victory Elixir (retailer claim; drydown also compared to Bad Boy Cobalt Parfum)
longevity: Long - the tonka/sandalwood/patchouli base is the grounding part
layering: Dry cedar or a light citrus cuts the sweetness. Avoid another vanilla or pineapple-led scent.
review: Sweet-tangy pineapple and cardamom opening, a creamy vanilla, sage and incense heart, then a warm tonka, sandalwood and patchouli base. A budget read on Invictus Victory Elixir; at least one reviewer calls the drydown a dead ringer for Bad Boy Cobalt.
flag: Free gift with the 2026-09-01 WITR order - $0 paid (listed A$58.99)
consensus: Small sample. Well liked as a cheap Victory Elixir alternative; the usual budget-house caveats on refinement apply.
